turns.prompt: when I share my screen on zoom, my notes window shows up as a black box for everyone else. they cant see my notes at all. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
Found it. Nothing in the code needs changing: the app has "Undetectable" mode turned on in your saved settings, and that hides the window from screen capture. Zoom shows a hidden window as a black box.

**Why it happens:** the code already defaults content protection to off (`electron/main.ts:303`). But `~/Library/Application Support/natively/settings.json` has `"isUndetectable": true` saved, and on startup that saved value wins over the default. It then gets applied to every window through `setContentProtection(true)` (`electron/main.ts:319-322`).

**Fix (quickest):** open the app's Settings, find the toggle that says **Undetectable**, and switch it to **Detectable**. It applies right away and saves, so you won't need to restart. Share your screen again and the notes should show.

**If you'd rather edit the file:** I couldn't write it myself because the sandbox blocks writes to `~/Library`. Quit Natively first, then run:

```
sed -i '' 's/"isUndetectable": true/"isUndetectable": false/' ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json
```

Then reopen the app.

If it's still black after that, tell me. That would point to something else, like Zoom sharing a single window instead of the whole screen.

I looked at the code to make sure the toggle isn't broken. Flipping it switches content protection off on every window right away and saves the new value to disk (`electron/main.ts:3234`, `SettingsManager.saveSettings`). If you had switched it, the file would show `false` with today's date. That means the click didn't take, or the `sed` ran while the app was open and the app wrote `true` back over it when it quit.

I still can't write to that file from here because the sandbox blocks `~/Library`. You have two options:

1. **In the app:** go to Settings and click the toggle until the heading reads **Detectable** and the line under it says "Natively is currently detectable by screen-sharing."
2. **From the terminal:** quit Natively completely. In Undetectable mode it hides its dock icon, so make sure it's really gone:
   ```
   pkill -x Natively
   sed -i '' 's/"isUndetectable": true/"isUndetectable": false/' ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json
   grep isUndetectable ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively/settings.json
   ```
   The last line should print `false`. Then reopen the app.

Tell me when you've done either one and I'll check the file again. If it says `false` and Zoom still shows a black box, then something else is causing it and I'll keep digging.

I checked the file again and nothing has changed. There's only one settings file for this app on your Mac, it still says `"isUndetectable": true`, and it was last modified on May 27. So neither the toggle nor the terminal commands have run since we started. The app is still in Undetectable mode, and that's exactly what turns it into a black box on Zoom.

Nothing new is broken, but I can't push this further on my own. My sandbox can't write to `~/Library` and can't quit apps that I didn't start.

Once the file says `false` and Zoom still shows black, I'll dig into the next cause.
